revision_instructions: Item 11: The sentence 'For a compliance team of 10 analysts, moving document extraction and initial risk scoring to the Automate layer recovers an estimated 4–6 analyst days per week for Adjudicate work that carries genuine regulatory accountability.' makes a specific quantitative claim ('4–6 analyst days per week') with no source. Fix ONE of these three ways: (A) Replace the estimate with a sourced statistic about AI time-savings in compliance operations — for example, if you can reference a named source for time recovered by automating document extraction or risk scoring workflows, cite it; OR (B) Reframe as Payal's direct operational experience by attributing explicitly to her advisory work: e.g. 'Based on delivery programmes I have run at Mastercard and in my advisory work, a compliance team of 10 analysts moving document extraction and initial risk scoring to the Automate layer typically recovers 4–6 analyst days per week...' — this makes it expert testimony, not an unsourced data point; OR (C) Remove the specific quantitative estimate entirely and replace with a structural statement that does not make a quantitative claim: e.g. 'For a compliance team of 10 analysts, the shift frees significant analyst capacity from extraction work to the Adjudicate-layer tasks that carry genuine regulatory accountability — the headcount stays flat, but the judgment density of the work rises.' Do not add or fabricate any new external source. Do not change any other part of the article. Fix only this sentence.
